input: Root's runtime summary: Darwin live, no panic. PDM1SPIHID transport works with valid CRCs. Stop 'device-metadata' error -2 (M1KBD_BOARD). Last packet flags 40 device d0 offset 0 remain 0 length 99, parser_error 0. Last message flags 40 device d0 command 20 report 01 subdevice d0 id 0, response_length 0, payload_length 89. Two identical stop logs. No human typing. The capture directory itself was not inspected.
established: SPI power, pinmux, controller, spien reset, boot notification, the write path with ac 27 68 d5 status, the read path, packet and message CRCs, and the root protocol engine all worked on real hardware: a CRC-valid device-info response came back.

Response identity is right: device d0, flags 40, command 20, report 01, subdevice d0, and the request id 0 echoed. m1kbd_response_matches passed, so this K1 risk (device 0xd0 and id echo) is now resolved.
packet length 99 = 8-byte header + 89-byte payload + 2-byte message CRC. A single packet, so no reassembly was involved.

failing_check.where: m1kbd_hid.c m1kbd_device_info (returns -1, so PDM1SPIHID calls fail(M1KBD_BOARD, 'device-metadata'))
excluded: vendor != 0x05ac or product != 0x0341: Linux on this machine reads vendor and product from the same offsets (6 and 8, struct spihid_device_info) and exposes 001C:05AC:0341, so these pass (strong inference).

remaining_candidates_ranked.why: The reference accepts any count >= 3 and clamps counts above 4 with 'limiting the number of devices to 4' (core.c:555-570). That branch exists because devices can report more than 4. This driver rejects > 4.

remaining_candidates_ranked.check: a string descriptor (offset,length at 12, 16 or 20) does not fit within 89 bytes
remaining_candidates_ranked.why: The reference silently skips an out-of-range string copy (core.c:575-606), and Linux never shows these strings, so their layout has never been proven. This driver fails hard. 89 - 24 = 65 bytes would fit three short strings, so this is less likely than rank 1, but if the offsets were relative to the message start rather than the payload, they would overrun by 8.

duplicate_logs.explanation: IOService::publishResource does gIOResources->setProperty and then registerService (IOService.cpp:5171-5185). Every resource publish (IOKit, IOBSD, IOConsoleUsers seed, ...) re-matches the drivers whose provider is IOResources. Once the first PDM1SPIHID instance fails start and detaches, its IOMatchCategory is free, so a new instance is created and repeats the whole power, reset and enumeration sequence. An identical id 0 and identical diagnostics fit a fresh instance.
duplicate_logs.consequence: This defeats 'no automatic retry': the hardware sequence can run once per resource publish. Each run is bounded and ends with spien low, so it is safe but unintended.
duplicate_logs.fix: Add a kext-global once-only latch, set atomically in probe() before returning this, so later instances refuse. Record the attempt count in a property.

recommended_next_revision: device_info: keep the exact 05ac:0341 identity gate. Accept num_devices >= 3 like Linux and record values above 4 (only interface 1 is used). Do not fail on string descriptors: the driver never uses the strings, so record an out-of-range flag instead.

Diagnostics: on a device-metadata or interface-metadata stop, IOLog the decoded fixed header: u0[0], u0[1], num_devices, vendor, product, version, and the three (offset,length) pairs. For interface info: interface_num, country, max_in/out/ctrl, and the name (offset,length). None of these are string bytes or serial material.
interface_info has the same strictness pattern. Relax its name-string bound the same way and log interface_num before requiring 1, so the next run does not stop one step later with no detail.

Root, optional and read-only on Linux: grep the kernel log for 'limiting the number of devices' or 'Device info reports' from spi-hid-apple. A 'limiting' line would confirm rank 1 without another Darwin boot.
not_claimed: No keyboard input or typing. The run never reached the interface/descriptor requests or IOHID publication.
